## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dhammacakkakathā* ("Discussion of the Wheel of the Teaching") is a text found within the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 2.7) [SuttaCentral]. In its doctrinal exposition, it itemizes spiritual faculties and factors of enlightenment, formulating their activation with phrases such as "the faculty of trust is *dhamma*, he sets that *dhamma* in motion" (*saddhindriyaṃ dhammo, taṃ dhammaṃ pavatteti*) [Gethin 2001].
SuttaCentral relates the text thematic- and textually to the foundational *Dhammacakkappavattanasutta* (SN 56.11), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4, Ne 14), and the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 20.6), as well as cross-traditional parallels including the Tibetan *Dharma-cakra-pravartana-sūtra* (D 31), Sanskrit witnesses in the *Lalitavistara* (chapter 26) and the *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and Chinese translations such as T 109 and T 1450.6 [SuttaCentral].
Computational analysis by DharmaNexus records 1,616 matching Pali passages across 59 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest internal overlaps occur with the adjacent *Paṭisambhidākathā* (Ps 2.6; over 36,000 shared characters), followed by the *Iddhipāda Saṃyutta* (SN 51), *Sacca Saṃyutta* (SN 56), *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṃyutta* (SN 47), the opening *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 14) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus include matches with the Sanskrit *Lalitavistara* (concurring with SuttaCentral), Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, the *Daśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*, the *Dharmasaṃgraha*, and the Chinese *San zhuan falun jing* (T 110) [DharmaNexus].
